Programs Read more In August 1996, Kathmandu University (K.U.) opened a Department of Music in Bhaktapur, where ethnomusicology (B.A. and M.A.) and practical music (North Indian classical and Nepalese local traditions) are taught to Nepalese and foreign students. The then German President, Dr. Roman Herzog, inaugurated the department during his state visit to Nepal on 29th November 1996. The academic courses are conducted by an experienced ethnomusicologist from Germany and lecturers from the U.S. and Nepal. Teaching staff for performance training includes local musicians and dancers. Department of Music ... --> Read more Center for Art and Design (KU Art+Design) - with a very short yet impressive history is committed towards establishing a benchmark in fine art education in Nepal. Realizing this need for qualitative fine art education in Nepal, Kathmandu University established Art and Design program in 2003 under School of Arts. With the initiation of key person Mr. Aidan Warlow, Director, M.A, Oxford, along with two other faculty members Mr. Rabindra Puri, M.A. Bremen and Mr. Sujan Chitrakar, M.F.A. New Delhi, and an assistant administrative staff Mr. Gopal Magar, a one-year Diploma course in Fine Arts was launched. Set up on the top floor that was rented off of a public school in a historic vicinity of Durbar Square, Bhaktapur, the first batch comprised of only six students. Department of Arts and Design ... --> Read more Bachelor in Media Studies (BMS) is an intensive four-year program offered under the Department of Languages and Mass Communication. It consists of all-encompassing courses with scope for concentration in a specialized field such as journalism, radio production, television production and film production, marketing communications, new media, media research, and so on. Department of Languages and Mass Communication ... --> Read more The graduate program in Human and Natural Resources Studies (HNRS) at Kathmandu University (KU) currently offers Master&rsquo;s and PhD degrees. These are research-oriented professional degrees that seek to impart research and analytical abilities necessary to understand the structure and functioning of rural society and their natural resource base. Department of Development Studies ... --> Read more The Department of Economics at Kathmandu University is dedicated to advancing the study of economic theory, applied research, and policy analysis. It offers a dynamic academic environment that fosters critical thinking, data-driven inquiry, and problem-solving skills relevant to contemporary socio-economic challenges. With experienced faculty and strong engagement in both national and global issues, the department provides students with rigorous training, practical exposure, and research opportunities. Currently, the department offers two programs: the Bachelor in Economics (B.Econ) and the Master in Economics (MECON), designed to prepare graduates for impactful careers in academia, policy-making, development, and related professional fields. Programs Read more In August 1996, Kathmandu University (K.U.) opened a Department of Music in Bhaktapur, where ethnomusicology (B.A. and M.A.) and practical music (North Indian classical and Nepalese local traditions) are taught to Nepalese and foreign students. The then German President, Dr. Roman Herzog, inaugurated the department during his state visit to Nepal on 29th November 1996. The academic courses are conducted by an experienced ethnomusicologist from Germany and lecturers from the U.S. and Nepal. Teaching staff for performance training includes local musicians and dancers. Department of Music ... --> Read more Center for Art and Design (KU Art+Design) - with a very short yet impressive history is committed towards establishing a benchmark in fine art education in Nepal. Realizing this need for qualitative fine art education in Nepal, Kathmandu University established Art and Design program in 2003 under School of Arts. With the initiation of key person Mr. Aidan Warlow, Director, M.A, Oxford, along with two other faculty members Mr. Rabindra Puri, M.A. Bremen and Mr. Sujan Chitrakar, M.F.A. New Delhi, and an assistant administrative staff Mr. Gopal Magar, a one-year Diploma course in Fine Arts was launched. Set up on the top floor that was rented off of a public school in a historic vicinity of Durbar Square, Bhaktapur, the first batch comprised of only six students. Department of Arts and Design ... --> Read more Bachelor in Media Studies (BMS) is an intensive four-year program offered under the Department of Languages and Mass Communication. It consists of all-encompassing courses with scope for concentration in a specialized field such as journalism, radio production, television production and film production, marketing communications, new media, media research, and so on. Department of Languages and Mass Communication ... --> Read more The graduate program in Human and Natural Resources Studies (HNRS) at Kathmandu University (KU) currently offers Master&rsquo;s and PhD degrees. These are research-oriented professional degrees that seek to impart research and analytical abilities necessary to understand the structure and functioning of rural society and their natural resource base. Department of Development Studies ... --> Read more The Department of Economics at Kathmandu University is dedicated to advancing the study of economic theory, applied research, and policy analysis. It offers a dynamic academic environment that fosters critical thinking, data-driven inquiry, and problem-solving skills relevant to contemporary socio-economic challenges. With experienced faculty and strong engagement in both national and global issues, the department provides students with rigorous training, practical exposure, and research opportunities. Currently, the department offers two programs: the Bachelor in Economics (B.Econ) and the Master in Economics (MECON), designed to prepare graduates for impactful careers in academia, policy-making, development, and related professional fields. Mathematics Education, existing MPhil Mathematics Education, and the proposed MPhil STEAM Education. STEAM Department was established in 2019. The STEAM department was established with the aim to develop and launch academic programs in the areas of Mathematics Education, Science Education, Technology Education, and STEAM Education. The department also aims to conduct research activities in the field of STEAM Education. In addition to this, the Department organizes short terms teacher professional programs to educate on innovative pedagogical approaches. There are different programs under this department that develop critical and creative human resources that can transform educational practices at different levels. &bull; Ph.D. in STEAM Education &bull; M Phil in STEAM Education &bull; One-Year MEd in STEAM Education &bull; MEd in Mathematics Education &bull; PGDE in Mathematics Education &bull; Graduate Diploma in Higher Education The department has developed new programs and contributed to developing human resources for the education sector, which is also one of the aims of the School. Also, the department has made a remarkable achievement in research and publication through the faculty. Graduate students from this department are engaged in several areas; teachers, teacher educators, and researchers. Their working culture and productivity in the workplace have become a remarkable reflection of the department. Department of STEAM Education Tracer Study Report 2014... --> Read more The Department of Inclusive Education, Early Childhood Development and Professional Studies (DIEP) received approval in November 2024 from the Academic Council and Executive Council, the principal decision-making bodies of the University. The establishment of the DIEP was founded upon the expansion of the Continuing and Professional Education Centre (CPEC), cultivated through extensive community education efforts within Kathmandu University School of Education. The depth of academic involvement, expansion of services, and potential for program innovation underscore the necessity of establishing the DIEP at KUSOED as a cross sectoral collaborative space focusing on research, innovation, and development. Message from the Coordinator Thank you for visiting the website of the Department of Inclusive Education, Early Childhood Development and Professional Studies (DIEP). DIEP is a cross sectoral learning space for adult learners on the cross cutting themes such as inclusion, special needs, ECD and professional learning who values collaboration, inclusion, empowerment, wellbeing, and entrepreneurship. KUSOED is composed of four departments and three functional centers, each dedicated to fostering academic growth and innovation. The school offers a wide range of programs, such as B Tech Ed in Information Technology, Post-Graduate Diploma, Master, MPhil, and PhD, catering to the diverse needs of its students. With over 800 current students and more than 1900 graduates, KUSOED has made significant strides in the field of education. The school is known for its community-driven and needs-based teacher education programs, which are designed to be impactful for their workplaces. KUSOED calls for admissions into MPhil and PhD programs in November/December and Bachelor and Master programs in May/June. We also run a university teacher education program for those who aspire to be trained faculty for higher educational institutions. You can check this out on our website. KUSOED is also at the forefront of educational and social research, contributing valuable insights and advancements in the field of education and society. The list of publications by faculty and students showcases our School&rsquo;s research profile. The school employs a blended pedagogy for postgraduate programs, combining online and face-to-face learning for a comprehensive educational experience. For undergraduate students, the school uses a face-to-face and internship-based pedagogy, providing students with practical experience in their field of study. In his role, he strives to develop KUSOED into a center of excellence, focusing on research, teaching, service, and community engagement across Nepal. His leadership philosophy, which emphasizes &lsquo;enabling by redesign,&rsquo; has played a significant role in the institution's transformation, leading to an increase in student enrollment, faculty recruitment, and graduation rates. Under the leadership of Prof. Luitel, notable achievements have been realized at KUSOED. His efforts have led to the re-introduction of various programs, including the BTechEd in Information Technology, BA-BEd in English, and BEd in Chinese Major with an English Minor. Additional postgraduate programs have been established across the five departments of the School. His efforts have also extended KUSOED's outreach beyond Kathmandu, with undergraduate programs established in Sindhuli, Biratnagar, and Rupandehi. Prof. Luitel has emphasized the importance of teacher education within the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector, advocating for curricula that are context-based and aligned with both local needs and global standards. He has successfully formed research teams and attracted international students. In addition to his role as Dean, Prof. Luitel is committed to academic leadership and management excellence. He has worked to uphold academic standards and has introduced innovative educational strategies by fostering an academic audit culture within the School of Education. His management philosophy is rooted in principles of social justice, equity, and sustainability, viewing educational institutions as platforms for societal transformation. He emphasizes effective and collaborative planning, encouraging all departments and centers to develop their strategic plans and follow through. He also stands as a mentor to the faculty and academic leaders, inspiring innovative thoughts and actions. His thought leadership at KUSOED has helped it achieve a new height of academic excellence, often illustrated by our partners' and clients' appreciation for KUSOED's better teaching, better research, and better services. Prof. Luitel&rsquo;s research concentrates on transformative STEAM education, focusing on context-based practices that nurture critical thinking and creativity. He co-founded the International Transformative Education Research Network (ITERN), engaging over 100 scholars worldwide in collaborative research initiatives. His commitment to resource mobilization has facilitated significant growth and innovation at KUSOED, including the creation of centers that benefit local communities. Through strategic partnerships with national and international organizations, he has contributed to the development of various academic programs and community support initiatives, reinforcing KUSOED's standing as a leading institution in Nepal and beyond. Prof Luitel has co-authored and co-edited four books (and one is forthcoming) and published over 150 articles in peer-reviewed journals, focusing on participatory action research, STEAM education, and transformative education, among others. In recognition of his contributions, he has received awards, such as Nepal&rsquo;s Rastriya Shikshya Puraskar (2010), the Young Scientist Award (2012), and the Mathematical Sciences Excellence Award (2019), to name but a few. Educated in Nepal and Australia and having worked in Nepal, Australia and Portugal, Prof. Luitel is actively engaged in transformative educational research and advises on national curriculum development. He has led over 25 inter/national research projects funded by NORAD, World Bank and other agencies, aimed at enhancing educational landscapes. His global influence is reflected in his keynote addresses, collaborative research projects/publications, and mentorship of over 25 PhD graduates. A lifelong learner, he remains dedicated to research on transformative pedagogy, learners-centric curricula, and philosophizing everyday lifeworld with an emphasis on local, Eastern/Southern (without rejecting Eurocentric/Western/Northern) and indigenous knowledge systems. It is now more apparent than ever that universities, schools and communities need to understand and facilitate change in favor of meaning-centered, authentic, and inclusive educational systems, processes, and outcomes. Kathmandu University School of Education (KUSOED) has been working with communities since its inception 24 years ago. For us, communities are key sites for the demonstration of change for quality education for leadership, the mission that facilitated the establishment of Kathmandu University 3 decades ago. Our faculty and students are committed to working towards accomplishing the mission of the university through their engagement in research and learning. Our academic programs emphasize research that is driven by students' informed choice through a pool of multiple epistemological traditions arising from local and global practices. Likewise, we strive to promote change-seeking participatory pedagogies (experiential, reflective, critical) that enable faculty and students to reflect, critique and envision their praxis as educational change agents. Our rapidly evolving expertise in remote teaching has been demonstrated by the continuity of our educational activities during the pandemic. We aspire to grow more into blended pedagogy to help faculty and students maximize their learning with ICT tools apt for participatory pedagogical spaces. At KUSOED, we strive to develop our academic programs to demonstrate a unique blend of needs expressed by the community and futuristic orientation offered by local, regional, and international instruments and frameworks and the ongoing research of the scholarly communities. Our teaching and research programs on Sustainable Development, Technical and Vocational Education, STEAM Education, Educational Leadership, Language Education, etc., are responding to the timely need for the mission of KUSOED - transforming society through educational excellence - built on the collective experience of faculty and students committed to improving their workplaces, communities and beyond. In addition to our ongoing collaborations with universities, research organisations, and funding agencies of international repute, we plan to offer a fee waiver scheme for a few meritorious and needy international students undertaking their MPhil and Ph.D. studies at KUSOED. Although the admission call will be published in December every year, students seeking advice about their studies may contact relevant professors in advance. You may find their profiles from our website, http://kusoed.edu.np. Despite some of these accomplishments, we are humble at the core, for our growth and excellence are driven by the ethos of lifelong learning. We dearly welcome your comments and suggestions on our ongoing activities in person and/or by writing to: soed_dean@ku.edu.np Prof. Bal Chandra Luitel, PhD School of Education +977-1-5912524 Hattiban, Lalitpur, Nepal, Email: admin@kusoed.edu.np Navigation E-Library Contact us E-learning KU ISMS Useful Links Apply For Transcripts Downloads e-Resource Guideline for Teaching and Learning KU- Downloads KU Online registration © School of Education, Tel. +977-1-5912524, Fax: 6250

The association aims to develop a network among the graduates so as to contribute to the educational excellence of KUSoEd by coordinating and utilizing the talents and experiences of the graduates. A total of about 1400 students have graduated from KUSoEd including 110 PhDs, 300 MPhils, 600 MEds and 350 PGDs. KUSoEd offers programmes with specialization in Educational Leadership and Management, Development Studies, English Language Education, Mathematics Education, STEAM, and Sustainable Development. A total of about 1400 students have graduated from KUSoEd including 110 PhDs, 300 MPhils, 600 MEds and 350 PGDs. KUSoEd offers programmes with specialization in Educational Leadership and Management, Development Studies, English Language Education, Mathematics Education, STEAM, and Sustainable Development. The office of SW is a non-political body that represents educational activities and coordinates programs for the welfare of the students. It also assists international students in integrating into the University system and Nepali society. It also organizes classes on Nepali culture and Nepali language classes for international students on demand. The School of Education is a premium institution in higher education in the country. The School has been a choice for students from home and abroad for their academic excellence. The glorious academic achievement of the School during the COVID-19 pandemic made the School one of the most sought academic institutes in the region. The introduction of new academic programs attracted more national and international students. The number of international scholars has been increasing in recent years. In a new cultural set-up, many students face problems like visa extension, conducting field research, and accommodation. Catering to international students increases our international visibility and sends a positive message to the international academic community. Ultimately it enables us to impact global ranking as it functions under the Student Welfare Directorate of Kathmandu University and under the guidance of the Dean. Primarily, it addresses the issues of students enrolled at the School of Education. MAJOR ACTIVITIES Organizes seminars/ webinars and talk programs inviting imminent scholars from Nepal and abroad; Organizes workshops on contemporary issues; Encourages students to disseminate their research through seminars/ webinars/ conferences and publications; Facilitates students in integrating into the University system; Organizes programs to integrate into Nepali society for international students; Coordinates student exchange programs with international institutes. The formalization of the Student Welfare Council at the School of Education is justifiable. The formalization of the Council authorizes it to act independently to minimize students' problems. Addressing the issues of students, particularly international ones, creates a positive image of the School and the University in the international academic community. This positive image encourages the School and the University to get higher ranks in the global ranking. TITLE:About Alumni Network &#8211; Alumni Network
CONTENT:About Alumni Network &#8211; Alumni Network Skip to content +977-11-415100 a&#108;umni&#064;k&#117;&#046;ed&#117;&#046;&#110;&#112; KU, Dhulikhel Alumni Network at Kathmandu University Menu About ANKU Team Alumni School of Arts School of Education School of Engineering School of Law School of Management School of Medical Sciences School of Science Alumni Visits News &#038; Notices Contact Register About Alumni Network It is a well-known fact that Kathmandu University graduates have left an indelible impression in varied and diverse fields such as Science, Technology, Academics, Education, Management, Industry, Policy Formation, Governance, Social Science and Entrepreneurship not only within Nepal but overseas as well because of their enthusiasm for learning and making the world a better place to live in. Graduating from Kathmandu University, known for its academic excellence at home and abroad, our alumni have been setting up benchmarks, not only in top level government positions, but also in private sectors and abroad. Kathmandu University believes that the sustenance of the University depends on the social acceptance of its alumni and the contributions they make by converting the vision and mission of Kathmandu University into a reality. The vision statement of KU states, “…to become a world-class university devoted to bringing knowledge and technology to the service of mankind”. Its mission statement is “to provide quality education for leadership”. In this context, alumni have been playing an important and substantial role to actualize the vision and mission of the University. The Alumni Network Kathmandu University (ANKU) Statute is drafted and finalized strictly in accordance with the values, vision, and mission of Kathmandu University (KU). It scrupulously aims at keeping in touch with the university graduates and contributing one another to grow together. This is done mainly through the initiatives from fellow members of the student community have completed their formal degrees from the University. They also serve as platform to: enable members to contribute their Alma Mater, in this case, Kathmandu University, in whatever manner possible and facilitate interaction with Faculty and Students of parent institution in particular, and with Nepali society at large for the optimal utilization of their experiences, resources, and skills for social benefit. Establishment of an alumni network becomes imperative to achieve the avowed objectives of ensuring longevity, inclusiveness, productive activism, promise for constant expansion, and sustained efforts the University. This context, a task force has been constituted to prepare Policy & Procedure Guidelines (pending the approval in upcoming meeting by Executive Council) for operation the Central Alumni Network of Kathmandu University. The principal idea behind this exercise is bring together alumni consolidated network and establish channels of communication at central Headquarters of University. The task force has come into force from 17th May, 2020 for period of one year with the possibility of extension of tenure based on effective performance. The task force comprises 14 members under the chief patronage of Vice-Chancellor. The particulars of members the task force as under. Asst. Prof. Sudarshan Prasad Dahal (KUSOA) Asst. Prof. Dr. Tikaram Poudel (KUSOED) Asst. Prof. Dr. Balram Pokhrel (KUSOED) Full time Faculty Anup K. Acharya (KUSOL) Asst. Prof. Roshee Lamichhane (KUSOM) ( Coordinator) Asst. Prof. Dr. Ganga Ram Phaijoo (KUSOS) Asst. Prof. Kirti Kaushal Joshi (KUSOA) Asst Prof. Dr. Shesha Kanta Pangeni (KUSOED) Lecturer Vimesh Poudel (KUSOE) Santosh K.C. (KUSOL) Asst Prof. Srawan K.C. (KUSOM) Asst Prof. Paras Mani Timilsina (KUSOS) Kunta Pun ( KUSMS) Dr Ram Gurung (KUSMS) The task force has successfully been in operation and has initiated tracer study of graduates. Kafle, assistant professor at the Department of Chemical Science & Engineering... --> Read more Chemical Engineering : The chemical engineers are well-equipped to solve diverse kinds of problems with strong emphasis on inherent safety, economics, and sustainability of the solutions. They are equally adept at solving technical problems as well as handling the managerial challenges in the complex organizational systems. They are trained to conceptualize, design, construct, control, and optimize all kinds of processes and operations at industrial scale with utmost focus on quality, efficiency, economics, safety, system integration and sustainability. They are also responsible for controlling the pollution arising from the physical and chemical processes, and providing remediation measures for environmental problems. As the country&rsquo;s first autonomous, not-for-profit, self-funding public institution in Higher Education in Engineering programs, School of Engineering (SoE) at Kathmandu University paved the way and is now a world class engineering school that proudly represents our country Nepal in the global arena. We, SoE started our journey in Higher Education in Engineering Education with Computer Engineering, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering in 1994. Now we are stronger with Civil Engineering, Architecture Engineering, Chemical Engineering, and Geometric Engineering. We are strongly committed to focus on setting new standards of excellence in each of the following areas: Research that targets today&rsquo;s greatest societal challenges. Education that empowers students to become future change agents. Equal and equitable access for the many to succeed in Engineering careers. Entrepreneurship that helps bring great ideas to the global industry. It is no hidden that COVID 19 has taught us a lot of lessons, especially in higher education. Covid 19 has forced the entire globe into a new era with new challenges and new opportunities. Events during the Covid 19 have taught us a lot about the need for resilience, justice, and sustainability. Existing education system has to be rejuvenated for new challenges and new opportunities. Therefore, the School of Engineering has timely recognized a dire need to develop soft skills along with technical skills among learners for these new challenges and opportunities. We are steering our academic activities according to the need of education 4.0 for Industrial Revolution 4.0 and Society 5.0 Our collective effort in School of Engineering (SoE) is always directed to address the current global as well as local challenges and gain national and international respect as a SoE leading the future of all of us. Moreover, School of Engineering (SoE) at Kathmandu University has already taken a new direction to empower our students to be equipped with new skills to address the existing and future challenges and create an opportunity with high adaptability in new era with new vision &ldquo; To be a Center of Excellence in Higher Education in Engineering by 2026&rdquo;. Rapid learning, lifelong learning, unlearning, and adaptability are main mantras in our School of Engineering. Problem based learning, project-based learning, challenged based learning and active learning in engineering education is our approach for a new era. Our School of Engineering (SoE) is very much passionate about research. SoE is thriving for excellence both in fundamental contribution to academic knowledge, as well as in creating technology with practical impact in the community. Our research will be more on the issues of climate change, and sustainable development using the potentials of emerging technologies in every engineering field. We have a series of challenges and also piles of opportunities. Everything is possible if we unite together and work hard. Prof. Manish Pokharel, PhD Dean, School of Engineering School of Engineering +977-11-415100 Dhulikhel, Kavre, Email: soe_office@ku.edu.np Navigation ISMS e-Learning Useful Links Brochures Fact Sheets © School of Engineering, Tel. +977-11-415100, Fax: +977-11-415011

Mechanical EngineeringResearch ProgramsEnergize Nepal Home Technical Training Center Technical Training Center Kathmandu University Technical Training Centre had been established with a mission to fulfill the skilled workforce in context of advancing technologies in automobile and manufacturing sectors. It is an autonomous technical training institute operated by Kathmandu University and was established with financial and technical support from Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) to provide skill oriented training programs to under privileged youths. Mechanical EngineeringResearch ProgramsEnergize Nepal Home Research Programs Research Programs Following are the Research Activities at the School of Engineering: Department of Computer Science and Engineering Research Programs Dobhase Machine Translation Project Dr. Sanat Kumar Bista &ndash; Team Leader English to Nepali Rule Based Machine Translation System E-Government and Trust Issues Research works are underway at the Department of Computer Science and Engineering from Janaury 1, 2010 for surveying the e-readiness and trust related issues for the implementation of e-government in Nepal under the institutional grant awarded by the University Grants Commission (UGC), Nepal. Dr. Sanat Kumar Bista is the Principal Investigator of the Project whereas Mr. Bal Krishna Bal and Mr. Anup Banskota are the co-Investigators. The Project tenure is of 24 months. Research Lab Information and Language Processing Research Lab (ILPRL)Established in 2004, the ILPRL is basically focusing on conducting Research and Development in the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP). The Dobhase Project is an outcome of the ILPRL. Department of Mechanical Engineering Research Lab Turbine Testing Laboratory(TTL) Mr. Tore Skeie &ndash; Project Manager Mr. Raju Shrestha &ndash; Project Engineer Mr. Biraj Singh Thapa &ndash; Research Fellow Under construction with support from NORAD, TTL is expected to run in its full capacity by the end of 2011. The aim is to develop a center of excellence for the R&D of Hydraulic Machineries and back up the creation of a new turbine manufacturer in Nepal. For more information, visit:http://www.ku.edu.np/mech/water_power_laboratory/Turbine Testing Laboratory.htm Environmental Modeling Lab Kathmandu University, School of Engineering (SOE) has initiated action to work in the area of environmental pollution/climate change modeling using high speed parallel processing computers. Establishment and operation of an Environmental Modeling Lab (EML) is an ongoing process. Additional goal of this Environmental Modeling lab will be to enhance national human resource.s computational skills in the area of grid and distributed computing. SOE has already identified and delegated faculty members who will be working extensively in this area. Currently, Dr. Bhupesh Adhikary, chemical engineer, is leading a group of highly interdisciplinary faculty members to achive the goals of the lab. Other interested faculty/staff members within the University who are interested and match the goals of this lab are being identified and will be brought into the team. For more information, visit: http://soe.ku.edu.np/static-page/environmental-modeling-lab School of Engineering +977-11-415100 Dhulikhel, Kavre, Email: soe_office@ku.edu.np Navigation ISMS e-Learning Useful Links Brochures Fact Sheets © School of Engineering, Tel. +977-11-415100, Fax: +977-11-415011

Step 1 Disconnect your Apple device from your connected devices and iCloud. For detailed instructions, refer to the Removal Guide. Step 3 Receive the trade-in value of your device and immediately apply it towards the purchase of a new device. 1 / of 3 Please contact us at [email protected] if you have other enquiries. Trade-in program is provided by "Carousell". Frequently Asked Questions What do I need to bring along? You will be required to bring your charger and cable for laptops. What if I do not like the value after assessment? You can choose to not accept the trade-in value, but the value shown is final. Can multiple devices be traded in during the same transaction? Unfortunately, only one device can be traded in per transaction. Do I get to keep the memory card from the trade-in devices? We recommend that you remove and keep all your memory cards before you trade-in a device Would I be able to get back my old device back after the trade-in? You would not be able to retrieve your old device as all trade-ins are final. Prior to trading in your device, we recommend backing up all your important content such as contacts, photos, videos, etc. Can I trade-in my device if it does not work? We would not be able to assess your device if we are unable to power on your device. What if my device is not found in the trade-in device list? You can head down to our stores to get your device assessed by our iStudio Experts to check if it is accepted.
